findings.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Webhook auth is a bare `!==` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Unset → `undefined !== undefined` is false; empty string → `"" !== ""` is false — and `.env.example` ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` in this same diff. Either way an unauthenticated request falls through to a credential upsert for an arbitrary `userId`. Also not constant-time.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` sits *below* the `if (state?.teamId)` early-return, so it is only ever reached when `teamId` is falsy — it always runs as `{teamId: null}` and never guards a team install. The team branch checks only *accepted membership* (`prisma.team.findFirst`), so any accepted member can install a team-wide OAuth credential. Privilege escalation.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` assigns the zod **SafeParse wrapper** (`{success, data}`) to `credential.key`. The old line was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the data directly. Office365 (`:264`) and Salesforce (`:96`) both correctly unwrap `.data` — Google is the outlier. Corrupts every Google credential on refresh, in **default config**.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called but `prisma` is never imported in this file (imports end at `_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse`). Unbound identifier — `getClient()` throws for every Salesforce user. Build/runtime break, no flag gating.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — The two new helpers disagree on gating: `refreshOAuthTokens` requires `&& userId`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` does not. For a team credential (`userId === null`) with sync on, the **real provider** is called but the **minimal** schema is applied — stripping the response.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — When the response omits `refresh_token`, the code writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` as a sentinel, which callers then persist — destroying the real stored refresh token. Only Salesforce explicitly re-overrides it.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"` — the second overwrites the first. The schema validates only `access_token`, and zod strips everything else, so all provider fields (including expiry) are discarded in sync mode.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Sync branch returns a raw `Response`; the direct branch returns whatever the provider SDK returns. Callers are split: lark/office365/webex/msteams treat it as a `Response`, google/hubspot treat it as parsed data. The two branches are not interchangeable.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — `refreshFunction: () => any` and an untyped union return erase compile-time checking at all 7 call sites — this is the root cause that let #10 and #11 compile silently.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `const token = res?.data` — in sync mode `res` is a `Response`, which has no `.data`, so `token` is `undefined` and the next line throws on `token.access_token`.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 — In sync mode the `Response` is type-asserted to `HubspotToken`; `expiresIn` is `undefined`, so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN`, and the `Response` object itself is persisted as `credential.key`. Silently corrupts the credential.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — The new code refreshes the token and persists it, then builds `jsforce.Connection` from the **stale** `credentialKey.access_token` / `instance_url` — the refresh it just performed has no effect on the connection it was for.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `findFirst` on `(userId, appId)` with no `orderBy` and no uniqueness constraint. Users can hold multiple credentials per app (every OAuth connect calls `credential.create`), so the webhook overwrites a nondeterministic row — account A's credential can be replaced by account B's tokens. *Validated.*

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The outbound sync POST carries no auth header, signature, or shared secret — only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug`. An operator endpoint that trusts its payload lets anyone reaching it mint tokens for any user by iterating a small integer.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9 — Same `fetch` has no timeout/`AbortSignal` and never checks `response.ok`. A hung or 5xx sync endpoint stalls or silently poisons every OAuth refresh path.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — Because #7 strips `expires_in`, the spread rewrites the stale expired value back to the DB, and the freshness check reads exactly that field — so sync mode re-refreshes on every single request. *Validated.*

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` — reason phrases are not guaranteed (HTTP/2 omits them entirely), so a successful refresh can be rejected with an empty error message. `!response.ok` is the reliable check.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — Webex and Lark were wired to `refreshOAuthTokens` but **not** `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Webex's schema demands `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`; Lark reads a nested `data.data` envelope. Neither can be satisfied by the documented "access token and expiry" sync contract, and Lark's failure path deletes the credential. *Validated.*

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — No `req.method` gate (a GET reaches the handler), and `zod.parse` + `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse` are unwrapped — malformed input becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5 — `encodeOAuthState` parses `req.query.state` then re-stringifies it — a no-op round-trip that duplicates `decodeOAuthState` verbatim. It "encodes" nothing.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — A function named `parse` mutates its result by injecting a default. The side effect is invisible at every call site.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73 — The update writes only `key`, leaving `credential.invalid` set. That flag is written on unrecoverable refresh failure (`googlecalendar:113`, `webex:301`) with no visible path resetting it — a re-keyed credential stays flagged broken while the webhook returns 200. *Validated.*

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — The `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", ...)` diagnostic was deleted. Parse failures now surface as a generic message with no zod error and no provider body.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — `getClient()` now performs an unconditional token-refresh round-trip **and** a DB write with no expiry gate, where it previously did neither.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Webhook auth is a bare `!==` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Unset → `undefined !== undefined` is false; empty string → `"" !== ""` is false — and `.env.example` ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` in this same diff. Either way an unauthenticated request falls through to a credential upsert for an arbitrary `userId`. Also not constant-time.

adjudication.rationale: The handler’s auth check is `if (req.headers[headerName] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) return 403;`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (so `undefined`) and the request omits that header (so also `undefined`), the condition is false and the request is treated as authenticated, allowing credential create/update for an arbitrary `userId`/`appSlug`. Additionally, `.env.example` in this diff introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""`, and if a deployment copies that (empty secret) an attacker can send the header with an empty value to bypass the check (`"" !== ""` is false). The comparison is also not constant-time, though the primary issue is the missing/empty-secret bypass.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` is declared as `async (refreshFunction: () => any, ...)` and returns either `fetch(...)` (a `Response`) or the result of `refreshFunction()` (provider-specific types). Because both the callback and the function’s return are effectively `any`/`Promise<any>`, TypeScript will not type-check callers. This is directly observable at call sites in the diff (e.g., HubSpot assigns `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` to `HubspotToken`, but in the credential-sync branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response`, which would be a runtime type mismatch that TS won’t catch due to `any`). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, which conditionally POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with a body containing only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` and sets no authentication material (no shared-secret header, signature, token, etc.). This is directly verifiable in the added code. While the impact depends on how the operator’s endpoint is exposed/implemented, the helper provides no mechanism to authenticate Cal.com to that endpoint, making the finding (missing auth on the outbound sync call) a real issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9 — Same `fetch` has no timeout/`AbortSignal` and never checks `response.ok`. A hung or 5xx sync endpoint stalls or silently poisons every OAuth refresh path.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — Because #7 strips `expires_in`, the spread rewrites the stale expired value back to the DB, and the freshness check reads exactly that field — so sync mode re-refreshes on every single request. *Validated.*

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` — reason phrases are not guaranteed (HTTP/2 omits them entirely), so a successful refresh can be rejected with an empty error message. `!response.ok` is the reliable check.
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: the OAuth refresh handler checks `response.statusText` (reason phrase) instead of the reliable `response.ok`, which can misclassify successful responses and cause refresh failures/stale credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — Webex and Lark were wired to `refreshOAuthTokens` but **not** `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Webex's schema demands `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`; Lark reads a nested `data.data` envelope. Neither can be satisfied by the documented "access token and expiry" sync contract, and Lark's failure path deletes the credential. *Validated.*

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88` and claims specific Webex schema requirements, but the diff provided does not include any Webex file changes (or even that file), so that portion is not verifiable from the diff. For Lark, the diff shows it was wired to `refreshOAuthTokens`, but there is no evidence in the diff that Lark should use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (Lark’s refresh flow uses `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)` and not a zod schema parse). The finding’s additional assertions (that Lark expects a `data.data` envelope and that its failure path deletes the credential) are not shown in the diff, so they cannot be validated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — No `req.method` gate (a GET reaches the handler), and `zod.parse` + `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse` are unwrapped — malformed input becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that `zod.parse` is unwrapped and that malformed input results in an unhandled 500 instead of a 400, which is the same core issue as the golden comment (schema `parse` throwing on invalid payloads leading to 500s). It adds extra concerns (missing `req.method` gate, decrypt/JSON.parse), but still matches the expected underlying problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — A function named `parse` mutates its result by injecting a default. The side effect is invisible at every call site.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after `safeParse` succeeds the function conditionally mutates the parsed output: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the provider response lacks `refresh_token` (line ~25). This means callers that read `tokenResponse.data.refresh_token` cannot distinguish a real refresh token from an injected placeholder, and this behavior is not apparent from the function name/signature at the call sites (e.g., Office365 uses `tokenResponse.data` to merge into stored credentials).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73 — The update writes only `key`, leaving `credential.invalid` set. That flag is written on unrecoverable refresh failure (`googlecalendar:113`, `webex:301`) with no visible path resetting it — a re-keyed credential stays flagged broken while the webhook returns 200. *Validated.*

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the webhook handler updates an existing credential with `data: { key: keys }` and creates a credential without mentioning any `invalid` field. However, the proposed finding hinges on (1) a `credential.invalid` column existing and (2) it being set elsewhere on refresh failure (citing `googlecalendar:113`, `webex:301`). Neither the presence of an `invalid` flag nor any code that sets it is shown in this diff (the only Prisma updates shown here also update `key` only). Therefore the claim that a “re-keyed credential stays flagged broken” is not verifiable from the provided changes and relies on out-of-diff assumptions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `if (!tokenResponse.success) { console.error(...) }` block in `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and replaces `safeParse` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure. However, this is an observability/debugging regression rather than a clear correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the diff, and it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that failures “surface” without any other logging (they may be caught/logged elsewhere).
